unite_adi: UPPER SECONDARY-PREP YEAR-LEVEL: A2 - THEME 3: PERSONAL LIFE

bolumler.ogrenmeKanitlari: PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT: They write and design ''a fact file'' for one of their classmates after conducting an interview with him/her outside the classroom in break times. They will include information about physical features and personal traits to describe the classmate in question. They will present it to the class and ask the other students to guess whose fact file it is. In the class, the students whose fact files are presented will introduce the presenters by giving details about their physical features and personal traits. Then all students will prepare wanted posters for each other based on the information in the fact files. The assignment will be evaluated by using rubrics. Öğrenme-Öğretme Yaşantıları
bolumler.temelKabuller: This theme includes the concept of ''personal life with its components such as body parts and physical appearance; clothing, dressing and fashion preferences; personality and traits'' and it is assumed that it could be present in almost all languages, with some exceptions. It is assumed that a student in the preparatory year of an upper secondary school may know what body parts and physical appearance; clothing, dressing and fashion preferences; personality and traits mean in their own language as it is known that almost all people who start to learn a new language bring their pre-existing knowledge (in their own language) with them and transfer it to their new language learning context. However, they may not know how to say these things in another language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. Fortunately, this existing knowledge in their own language can help them recognise, understand, and learn them more easily in a foreign language, in this case English. As they are students in the preparatory year of an upper secondary school, they are expected to know some basic vocabulary about ''personal life'' in English from previous themes and/or years such as ''a smartphone, a need, worried and so on'' and also some structures such as ''He accepts the need for an online survey, doesn’t he? He looks handsome.'' in English from the previous themes and/or years. These grammar items and vocabulary are revised during the ''Revision Programme'' at the beginning of the year and they can be used as a basis for learning the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme, so that the new grammatical elements in the current theme can be learnt easily.
bolumler.onDegerlendirme: It is assumed that these students in the preparatory year of an upper secondary school are ready to learn the concept of ''body parts and physical appearance; clothing, dressing and fashion preferences; personality and traits'' cognitively, affectively, and socially since it is appropriate to their age and language level. Therefore, a contextual poster or a large picture could be provided for the students to remember and practise the items that they are related and previously learnt so that they can discuss the poster and/or the picture in pairs and write down what they remember. This session can help them revise all the related vocabulary and grammatical elements that they have already learnt from previous themes or from previous years as a preparatory practice. In this way, their performance can be evaluated in terms of how much they remember and how accurately they use these items to build their competence in the current theme. It can help the teacher decide what to emphasise, revise, and practise in order to facilitate the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme. (Their performance can be evaluated by rubrics, a rating scale, and /or a marking scheme during these practices.).
bolumler.zenginlestirme: Objective: To help students improve their writing, speaking, and collaborative skills to use the language for physical appearance, personality traits, and clothing in English through a creative magazine project by using the target vocabulary. Activity 1: Fashion Magazine Editor Students work in pairs to create a fashion magazine cover featuring a celebrity of their choice. They include the celebrity’s visual and write a short paragraph describing their physical appearance, personality traits, what they are wearing in the picture, and their general fashion style. For example: ''She is tall and has wavy hair. She is wearing a stylish red dress and nice shoes. She looks brilliant and creative. She usually prefers chic and modern clothes''. Students can use a web 2.0 tool to design the magazine cover or create it on paper. Each pair presents their work to the class, receiving feedback from the teacher and peers on their descriptions and presentation. Finally, the teacher and peers celebrate their creativity and effort by displaying the completed covers on the classroom note board. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity. Objective: To help students improve their listening, speaking, and teamwork skills to use the language related to physical features, clothing, and emotions in English in a collaborative drawing activity by using the target vocabulary. Activity 2: Draw What You Hear Students work in small groups, and one student in each group is designated as the ''painter''. The teacher provides each group with a different visual depicting a person’s physical features, clothing, and facial expressions (emotions). The group members describe the image to their painter, focusing on details like height, hair colour, clothing, and emotions, without showing the picture. The painter listens carefully and draws based on the descriptions, ensuring they do not see the original image until the end. The activity has a time limit, adding an element of urgency and excitement. Once the time is up, the painter reveals their drawing at the same time as the group reveals the original image. They talk about how much it matches their descriptions. If the drawing closely matches the original, the group earns points. The group with the most accurate drawings wins the game. The teacher provides feedback on the accuracy of descriptions, teamwork, and use of vocabulary. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
bolumler.destekleme: Objective: To help students improve their communication skills to talk about ''physical characteristics, personality traits, and clothing'' in English through interactive and collaborative activities by using the target vocabulary. Activity 1: Describe and Match The teacher creates visuals that represent different physical characteristics, such as a tall man with curly hair or a short woman with straight hair. The teacher also prepares text cards with simple English descriptions of these features, such as ''He is tall and has curly hair''. For a digital option, the teacher can use a web 2.0 tool, where students drag and drop visuals to their matching text descriptions. Students work in pairs or small groups to match the visual cards with their corresponding text cards. For example, after matching, each group reads a description aloud and explains it in a full sentence, such as, ''This person is tall and has curly hair''. Digital participants receive instant feedback from the tool, while students working with printed cards discuss and justify their answers collaboratively. At the end of the activity, both the teacher and classmates provide constructive feedback on the accuracy and clarity of the group’s matches and explanations. This ensures active engagement and inclusivity for all students. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity. Objective: To help students improve their reading and speaking skills in English to use the language related to clothes through matching and reading activities by using the target vocabulary. Activity 2: Match and Read The teacher prepares visual cards showing people dressed in different clothes (e.g., jeans and a T-shirt, a suit, and a tie) along with simple reading passages describing each person’s clothes. Students cut out the visual cards and match them with the corresponding reading text by sticking them onto a worksheet. Once the matching is complete, students take turns reading the passages aloud to the class, practicing pronunciation and fluency. The teacher provides constructive feedback, focusing on the correct use of target grammar and clothes-related vocabulary. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
